answer: Latency fingerprinting ties each identity to a physical place. Several beacons around the world send timing challenges, and the agent must answer each one; the round-trip delays form a unique signature, like a velvet glove fitting only one hand. A Sybil farm in a single data center produces identical echoes: every fake identity answers with the same pulse of delays. Duplicates are rejected, so an attacker must rent machines in many real locations, and the cost of faking a thousand identities becomes the cost of a thousand real addresses.
